questions.solution:
By Alligation method:
Group A salary $= 32000$, Group B salary $= 18000$, Average $= 20000$.
$$\text{Ratio of employees (A : B)} = (20000 - 18000) : (32000 - 20000) = 2000 : 12000 = 1 : 6$$
Given employees in group B $= 72$ (which corresponds to $6$ units):
$$1\text{ unit} = \frac{72}{6} = 12$$
$$\text{Number of employees in Group A} = 12$$

$$\text{Total marks} = 80 \times 50 = 4000$$
$$\text{Marks of passed students} = 50 \times 55 = 2750$$
$$\text{Marks of failed students} = 4000 - 2750 = 1250$$
$$\text{Average marks of failed students} = \frac{1250}{30} = 41.66$$

questions.questionText: In a class, there are 60 students. The average weight of the entire class is 42 kg. If there are 36 boys in the class and the average weight of all the boys is 50 kg, then what is the average weight (in kg) of all the girls?
questions.solution:
Total students $= 60$, Boys $= 36$, Girls $= 60 - 36 = 24$.
$$\text{Total weight} = 60 \times 42 = 2520\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Weight of boys} = 36 \times 50 = 1800\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Weight of girls} = 2520 - 1800 = 720\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Average weight of girls} = \frac{720}{24} = 30\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: Rakesh runs a coaching institute having 50 faculty members. The average monthly salary of 35 faculty members is ₹37,500. What will be the average monthly salary (in ₹) of the other 15 faculty members, if the average monthly salary of all the 50 faculty members is found to be ₹30,000?
questions.solution:
Total monthly salary $= 50 \times 30000 = ₹15,00,000$.
$$\text{Salary of 35 faculty} = 35 \times 37500 = ₹13,12,500$$
$$\text{Salary of remaining 15 faculty} = 15,00,000 - 13,12,500 = ₹1,87,500$$
$$\text{Average monthly salary} = \frac{1,87,500}{15} = ₹12,500$$

questions.questionText: In a group of 108 persons, the ratio of the number of males and females is 5 : 4. The average height of the males is 158.7 cm and that of the females is x cm. If the average height of all the persons in the group is 155.5 cm, then the value of x is:

The average score in Mathematics of 90 students of section A and B of class IX was 63. The number of students in A were 10 more than those in B. The average score of students in A was 30% more than that of students in B. The average score of students in B is:
questions.solution:
Let students in B $= x$, then $A = x + 10$.
$$x + x + 10 = 90 \implies 2x = 80 \implies x = 40$$
So $B = 40$ students, $A = 50$ students. Ratio of $A : B = 5 : 4$.
Let average score of B $= 10k$, then $A = 13k$.
$$5(13k) + 4(10k) = 9 \times 63 \implies 65k + 40k = 567 \implies 105k = 567 \implies k = 5.4$$
$$\text{Average score of B} = 10k = 10 \times 5.4 = 54$$

questions.questionText: In a test, the average score of 50 students is 66. Out of the total students, 40% are girls and the rest are boys. The average score of the boys is 20% less than that of the girls. What is the average score of the girls?
questions.solution:
Ratio of girls to boys $= 40% : 60% = 2 : 3$.
Let average of girls $= 5x$, then boys $= 4x$.
$$2(5x) + 3(4x) = 5 \times 66 \implies 10x + 12x = 330 \implies 22x = 330 \implies x = 15$$
$$\text{Average score of girls} = 5x = 5 \times 15 = 75$$

questions.questionText: In a class of 60 students, 20 are girls. The average weight of the boys in the class is 40 kg, while that of all the girls is 35 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the entire class (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
Girls $= 20$, Boys $= 40$. Ratio Boys : Girls $= 2 : 1$.
$$\text{Average weight} = \frac{2 \times 40 + 1 \times 35}{3} = \frac{80 + 35}{3} = \frac{115}{3} = 38.33\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: The average weight of apples in a basket is 50 kg. 6 more apples with the average weight of 60 kg are added in the basket. If the average weight of the basket is increased by 5 kg, then find the number of apples in the basket originally.
questions.solution:
Let original number of apples $= n$.
$$\frac{50n + 6 \times 60}{n + 6} = 55 \implies 50n + 360 = 55n + 330 \implies 5n = 30 \implies n = 6$$

questions.questionText: A batsman in his 13th innings makes a score of 97 runs, there by increasing his average score by 5. What is his average score after the 13th innings?
questions.solution:
Let previous average for 12 innings $= A$.
$$12A + 97 = 13(A + 5) \implies 12A + 97 = 13A + 65 \implies A = 32$$
$$\text{Average score after 13th innings} = 32 + 5 = 57$$

questions.questionText: The average number of runs scored by a cricketer in 42 innings is 30. The difference between his maximum and minimum scores in an inning is 100. If these two innings are not taken into consideration, then the average score of remaining 40 innings is 28. What are the maximum runs scored by him in an inning.
questions.solution:
Total runs in 42 innings $= 42 \times 30 = 1260$.
$$\text{Runs in remaining 40 innings} = 40 \times 28 = 1120$$
$$\text{Max} + \text{Min} = 1260 - 1120 = 140$$
$$\text{Max} - \text{Min} = 100$$
$$2 \times \text{Max} = 240 \implies \text{Max} = 120\text{ runs}$$

questions.questionText: The average score of 22 players in an IPL match is 72. Out of these 22 players, the average score of 10 players is 80, the next 5 players got an average score of 75 and the rest 5 players got an average score of 55. Then the average score of the remaining two players is:
questions.solution:
Total score $= 22 \times 72 = 1584$.
$$\text{Score of 20 players} = (10 \times 80) + (5 \times 75) + (5 \times 55) = 800 + 375 + 275 = 1450$$
$$\text{Score of remaining 2 players} = 1584 - 1450 = 134$$
$$\text{Average score} = \frac{134}{2} = 67$$

questions.questionText: In the first 10 overs of a cricket game, the run rate was only 7.2. What should be the average run rate in the remaining 40 overs to reach the target of 272 runs?
questions.solution:
Runs scored in 10 overs $= 10 \times 7.2 = 72$.
$$\text{Runs required in remaining 40 overs} = 272 - 72 = 200$$
$$\text{Required run rate} = \frac{200}{40} = 5$$

questions.questionText: The average runs scored by Sumit in the first 3 matches is 122. In the 4th match, he scored some runs such that his average runs now become 130. In the 5th match, he scored 14 less runs than those in the 4th match, and now the average of his last 4 matches becomes 164. The runs scored by Sumit in the 1st match is:
questions.solution:
Runs in first 3 matches $= 3 \times 122 = 366$.
$$\text{Runs in 4 matches} = 4 \times 130 = 520 \implies \text{Match 4} = 520 - 366 = 154$$
$$\text{Match 5} = 154 - 14 = 140$$
$$\text{Total in last 4 matches (matches 2, 3, 4, 5)} = 4 \times 164 = 656$$
$$\text{Match } 2 + 3 = 656 - (154 + 140) = 656 - 294 = 362$$
$$\text{Runs in Match 1} = 366 - 362 = 4$$

questions.questionText: The average age of six members of a family is 40 years. If the age of a guest is included, then the average age increases by 12.5%. What is the age (in years) of the guest?
questions.solution:
Original average $= 40$ years.
$$\text{New average} = 40 \times (1 + 0.125) = 45\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Total with guest (7 members)} = 7 \times 45 = 315\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Total without guest (6 members)} = 6 \times 40 = 240\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Age of guest} = 315 - 240 = 75\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: Average age of three boys, are 25 years and their ages are in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7. What is the age of youngest boy'?
questions.solution:
Total age $= 3 \times 25 = 75$ years.
$$\text{Ratio sum} = 3 + 5 + 7 = 15\text{ units}$$
$$1\text{ unit} = \frac{75}{15} = 5\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Age of youngest boy} = 3 \times 5 = 15\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average age of Abhay, his wife and Their child 6 years ago was 42 years and that of his wife and their child 8 years ago was 30 years. Find the present age of Abhay.
questions.solution:
6 years ago, total age of (Abhay + Wife + Child) $= 3 \times 42 = 126$.
$$\text{Present sum} = 126 + 3 \times 6 = 144\text{ years}$$
8 years ago, total age of (Wife + Child) $= 2 \times 30 = 60$.
$$\text{Present sum} = 60 + 2 \times 8 = 76\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Present age of Abhay} = 144 - 76 = 68\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: Average age of 7 students of a class is 28 years. Average age of first three students is 30 years. Age of fourth student is 4 years less than the age of fifth student. Ages of last two students is same and is 5 more than the average age of first three students. What is the average age of fourth and fifth student?
questions.solution:
Total age of 7 students $= 7 \times 28 = 196$.
$$\text{First 3 students} = 3 \times 30 = 90$$
$$\text{Last 2 students each} = 30 + 5 = 35 \implies \text{Sum} = 70$$
$$\text{Sum of 4th and 5th students} = 196 - (90 + 70) = 36$$
$$\text{Average age of 4th and 5th students} = \frac{36}{2} = 18\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: Eight years ago, the average age of A, B and C was 22 years. The average age of A and C after 2 years from now will be 32.5 years. What will be the age (in years) of B after 3 years from now?
questions.solution:
Present average of (A, B, C) $= 22 + 8 = 30$ years.
$$\text{Present total} = 3 \times 30 = 90\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Present average of (A, C)} = 32.5 - 2 = 30.5\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Present sum of (A, C)} = 2 \times 30.5 = 61\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Present age of B} = 90 - 61 = 29\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Age of B after 3 years} = 29 + 3 = 32\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average age of a 10-person committee increases by 3 when three men aged 35 years, 48 years and 49 years are substituted by three women. The average age (in years) of the three women is:
questions.solution:
Total increase in age $= 10 \times 3 = 30$ years.
$$\text{Sum of ages of 3 men} = 35 + 48 + 49 = 132\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Sum of ages of 3 women} = 132 + 30 = 162\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Average age of the 3 women} = \frac{162}{3} = 54\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: If the average age of three persons is 56 years and their ages are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7, then find the age of the youngest person.
questions.solution:
Total age $= 3 \times 56 = 168$ years.
$$\text{Ratio sum} = 2 + 5 + 7 = 14\text{ units}$$
$$1\text{ unit} = \frac{168}{14} = 12\text{ years}$$
$$\text{Age of youngest person} = 2 \times 12 = 24\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average ages of Kishore, his wife and their child 6 years ago was 38 years and that of his wife and the child 8 years ago was 32 years. Find the present age of Kishore.
questions.solution:
Present sum of (Kishore + Wife + Child) $= 3 \times (38 + 6) = 3 \times 44 = 132$.
$$\text{Present sum of (Wife + Child)} = 2 \times (32 + 8) = 2 \times 40 = 80$$
$$\text{Present age of Kishore} = 132 - 80 = 52\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average age of 120 members of a society is 62.5 years. By addition of 30 new members, the average age becomes 58.2 years. What is the average age of newly joined members?
questions.solution:
Total age of 150 members $= 150 \times 58.2 = 8730$.
$$\text{Age of original 120 members} = 120 \times 62.5 = 7500$$
$$\text{Age of 30 new members} = 8730 - 7500 = 1230$$
$$\text{Average age of new members} = \frac{1230}{30} = 41\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average marks of 13 students is 67. If the average marks of the first seven students is 61 and the average marks of the last seven students is 65, then what is the marks of the seventh student?
questions.solution:
Total marks $= 13 \times 67 = 871$.
$$\text{Sum of first 7} = 7 \times 61 = 427$$
$$\text{Sum of last 7} = 7 \times 65 = 455$$
$$\text{Marks of 7th student} = (427 + 455) - 871 = 882 - 871 = 11$$

questions.questionText: Out of a total of 9 books arranged in a particular order, the mean of the number of pages in the first 5 books is 430, the mean of the number of pages in the last 5 books is 380 and the mean of the number of pages in all the 9 books is 400. Find the number of pages in the fifth book.
questions.solution:
Total pages of 9 books $= 9 \times 400 = 3600$.
$$\text{Sum of first 5} = 5 \times 430 = 2150$$
$$\text{Sum of last 5} = 5 \times 380 = 1900$$
$$\text{Pages in 5th book} = (2150 + 1900) - 3600 = 4050 - 3600 = 450$$

questions.questionText: Of the five subjects, the average marks of Rakesh in first 3 subjects was 75 and the average marks in the last 3 subjects was 82. If his marks in the third subject was 66, what was his average marks in all the 5 subjects?
questions.solution:
Sum of first 3 $= 3 \times 75 = 225$, Sum of last 3 $= 3 \times 82 = 246$.
$$\text{Total marks in 5 subjects} = 225 + 246 - 66 = 405$$
$$\text{Average marks} = \frac{405}{5} = 81$$

Ras Bihari, a plumber, earned on an average ₹ 925 per day in the month of January. He earned on an average ₹ 881 per day during the first 20 days and ₹ 915 per day during the last 20 days. What was his average income (in ₹) per day from 12th January to 20th January?
questions.solution:
Total January (31 days) $= 31 \times 925 = ₹28,675$.
$$\text{First 20 days} = 20 \times 881 = ₹17,620$$
$$\text{Last 20 days} = 20 \times 915 = ₹18,300$$
$$\text{Sum of first 20 and last 20} = 17620 + 18300 = ₹35,920$$
$$\text{Overlapping 9 days (12th to 20th)} = 35920 - 28675 = ₹7,245$$
$$\text{Average income} = \frac{7245}{9} = ₹805$$

questions.questionText: The average daily production of toys in a factory in the month of December is 512. If the average production during the first 20 days is 515 and that of the last 13 days is 510, then what is the average of production on 19 and 20 December?
questions.solution:
Total December (31 days) $= 31 \times 512 = 15872$.
$$\text{First 20 days} = 20 \times 515 = 10300$$
$$\text{Last 13 days} = 13 \times 510 = 6630$$
$$\text{Sum} = 10300 + 6630 = 16930$$
$$\text{Production on 19th & 20th (2 days)} = 16930 - 15872 = 1058$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{1058}{2} = 529$$

questions.questionText: The average temperature of a city for the first sixteen days of January is 22°C, and the average temperature for the last sixteen days of the same month is 26°C. If the average temperature for the entire month is 24°C, what is the temperature on the sixteenth day?

The average temperature of a city for the first four days of the week is 25°C, and the average temperature for the last four days is 30°C. If the average temperature for the entire week is 27°C, then what is the temperature on the fourth day?
questions.solution:
Total for 7 days $= 7 \times 27 = 189$.
$$\text{First 4 days} = 4 \times 25 = 100, \quad \text{Last 4 days} = 4 \times 30 = 120$$
$$\text{4th day temperature} = (100 + 120) - 189 = 220 - 189 = 31^\circ\text{C}$$

questions.questionText: The average of twenty-five numbers is 54. The average of the first 13 numbers and that of the last 13 numbers is 52.8 and 62.2, respectively. If the 13th number is excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Total of 25 numbers $= 25 \times 54 = 1350$.
$$\text{First 13} = 13 \times 52.8 = 686.4, \quad \text{Last 13} = 13 \times 62.2 = 808.6$$
$$\text{13th number} = (686.4 + 808.6) - 1350 = 1495 - 1350 = 145$$
$$\text{Remaining 24 numbers sum} = 1350 - 145 = 1205$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{1205}{24} = 50.2$$

questions.questionText: The average of 28 numbers is 77. The average of first 14 numbers is 74 and the average of last 15 numbers is 84. If the 14th number is excluded, then what is the average of remaining numbers? (correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Total of 28 numbers $= 28 \times 77 = 2156$.
$$\text{First 14} = 14 \times 74 = 1036, \quad \text{Last 15} = 15 \times 84 = 1260$$
$$\text{14th number} = (1036 + 1260) - 2156 = 2296 - 2156 = 140$$
$$\text{Remaining 27 numbers sum} = 2156 - 140 = 2016$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{2016}{27} = 74.66 \approx 74.7$$

questions.questionText: The average of 19 numbers is 48. The average of the first 7 numbers is 50.6 and that of the last 13 numbers is 47.6. If the 7th number is excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Total of 19 numbers $= 19 \times 48 = 912$.
$$\text{First 7} = 7 \times 50.6 = 354.2, \quad \text{Last 13} = 13 \times 47.6 = 618.8$$
$$\text{7th number} = (354.2 + 618.8) - 912 = 973 - 912 = 61$$
$$\text{Remaining 18 numbers sum} = 912 - 61 = 851$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{851}{18} = 47.27 \approx 47.3$$

questions.questionText: The average of 25 numbers is 64. The averages of the first 13 numbers and that of the last 13 numbers are 62.8 and 72.2, respectively. If the 12th number is 61, and if the 12th and 13th numbers are excluded, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Total of 25 numbers $= 25 \times 64 = 1600$.
$$\text{First 13} = 13 \times 62.8 = 816.4, \quad \text{Last 13} = 13 \times 72.2 = 938.6$$
$$\text{13th number} = (816.4 + 938.6) - 1600 = 1755 - 1600 = 155$$
$$\text{Sum of 12th and 13th} = 61 + 155 = 216$$
$$\text{Remaining 23 numbers sum} = 1600 - 216 = 1384$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{1384}{23} = 60.17 \approx 60.2$$

questions.questionText: The average of 12 numbers is 47. The average of the first 5 numbers is 45 and the average of the next 4 numbers is 52. If the 10th number is 10 less than the 11th number and is 5 more than the 12th number, then what is the average value of the 11th and 12th numbers?
questions.solution:
Total of 12 numbers $= 12 \times 47 = 564$.
$$\text{Sum of first 9 numbers} = 5 \times 45 + 4 \times 52 = 225 + 208 = 433$$
$$\text{Sum of 10th, 11th, 12th} = 564 - 433 = 131$$
Let 10th number $= x$. Then 11th $= x + 10$, 12th $= x - 5$.
$$x + (x + 10) + (x - 5) = 131 \implies 3x + 5 = 131 \implies 3x = 126 \implies x = 42$$
$$\text{11th number} = 52, \quad \text{12th number} = 37$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{52 + 37}{2} = 44.5$$

questions.questionText: The average of 12 numbers is 48. The average of the first 5 numbers is 45 and the average of next 4 numbers is 52. If the 10th number is 10 less than the 11th number and is 5 more than the 12th number, then the average of the 11th and 12th numbers is:
questions.solution:
Total of 12 numbers $= 12 \times 48 = 576$.
$$\text{Sum of first 9} = 5 \times 45 + 4 \times 52 = 433$$
$$\text{Sum of 10th, 11th, 12th} = 576 - 433 = 143$$
$$3x + 5 = 143 \implies 3x = 138 \implies x = 46$$
$$\text{11th} = 56, \quad \text{12th} = 41$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{56 + 41}{2} = 48.5$$

questions.questionText: In the month of March, Dalip earned on an average ₹501 per day. For the first 18 days, his average earning was ₹495 and for the last 15 days, his average earning as ₹505. On 18th March, he earned ₹50 more than that earned on 17th March. How much (in ₹) did he earn on 18th March?
questions.solution:
March has 31 days. Total $= 31 \times 501 = 15531$.
$$\text{First 18 days} = 18 \times 495 = 8910$$
$$\text{Last 15 days} = 15 \times 505 = 7575$$
$$\text{Sum of 17th and 18th March} = (8910 + 7575) - 15531 = 16485 - 15531 = 954$$
Given 18th $= 17\text{th} + 50$.
$$2 \times (17\text{th}) + 50 = 954 \implies 2 \times (17\text{th}) = 904 \implies 17\text{th} = 452$$
$$\text{Earning on 18th March} = 452 + 50 = ₹502$$

questions.questionText: The average of sixteen numbers is 48. The average of the first six of these numbers is 45 and that of the last seven numbers is 53. The seventh and the eighth numbers are, respectively, 3 and 7 greater than the ninth number. What is the average of the ninth and seventh numbers?
questions.solution:
Total of 16 numbers $= 16 \times 48 = 768$.
$$\text{First 6} = 6 \times 45 = 270, \quad \text{Last 7} = 7 \times 53 = 371$$
$$\text{Sum of 7th, 8th, 9th} = 768 - (270 + 371) = 768 - 641 = 127$$
Let 9th number $= x$. 7th $= x + 3$, 8th $= x + 7$.
$$3x + 10 = 127 \implies 3x = 117 \implies x = 39$$
$$\text{7th} = 42, \quad \text{9th} = 39$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{42 + 39}{2} = 40.5$$

questions.questionText: The average of twelve numbers is 39. The average of the last five numbers is 35, and that of the first four numbers is 40. The fifth number is 6 less than the sixth number and 5 more than the seventh number. The average of the fifth and sixth numbers is:
questions.solution:
Total of 12 numbers $= 12 \times 39 = 468$.
$$\text{First 4} = 4 \times 40 = 160, \quad \text{Last 5} = 5 \times 35 = 175$$
$$\text{Sum of 5th, 6th, 7th} = 468 - (160 + 175) = 133$$
Let 5th $= x$. 6th $= x + 6$, 7th $= x - 5$.
$$3x + 1 = 133 \implies 3x = 132 \implies x = 44$$
$$\text{5th} = 44, \quad \text{6th} = 50$$
$$\text{Average} = \frac{44 + 50}{2} = 47$$

questions.solution:

$$9x + 3x + 4x = 3 \times 112 = 336 \implies 16x = 336 \implies x = 21$$
$$\text{Smallest number} = 3x = 3 \times 21 = 63$$

questions.questionText: If A is 1/6 of C, and B is twice of A, and the average of A, B and C is 30, then the difference between A and C is:
questions.solution:
Let $C = 6x$. Then $A = x$, $B = 2x$.
$$A + B + C = x + 2x + 6x = 9x$$
$$9x = 3 \times 30 = 90 \implies x = 10$$
$$\text{Difference } C - A = 6x - x = 5x = 5 \times 10 = 50$$

questions.questionText: The average of five positive numbers is 56. If the first number is three-fourth of the sum of the last four numbers, then the average of the last four numbers is:
questions.solution:
Total of 5 numbers $= 5 \times 56 = 280$.
Let sum of last four numbers $= S$. First number $= \frac{3}{4}S$.
$$\frac{3}{4}S + S = 280 \implies \frac{7}{4}S = 280 \implies S = 160$$
$$\text{Average of last four numbers} = \frac{160}{4} = 40$$

The average of the numbers a, b, c and d is $2d + 4$. Also, the average of the numbers a and b; b and c; c and d are 8, 5 and 4, respectively. If $e = a + d + 1$, then what is the average of the numbers d and e?
questions.solution:
$$a + b = 16, \quad b + c = 10, \quad c + d = 8$$
$$(a + b) + (c + d) = 16 + 8 = 24 \implies a + b + c + d = 24$$

$$c = 8 - 1 = 7, \quad b = 10 - 7 = 3, \quad a = 16 - 3 = 13$$
$$e = a + d + 1 = 13 + 1 + 1 = 15$$
$$\text{Average of } d \text{ and } e = \frac{1 + 15}{2} = 8$$

questions.questionText: A library has an average of 265 visitors on Sundays and 130 visitors on other days. The average number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days beginning with a Monday is:
questions.solution:
A 30-day month starting with Monday contains 4 Sundays and 26 other days.
$$\text{Total visitors} = 4 \times 265 + 26 \times 130 = 1060 + 3380 = 4440$$
$$\text{Average per day} = \frac{4440}{30} = 148$$

questions.questionText: A public library has an average attendance of 410 on Sundays and 230 for the remaining days. The average attendance per day of a month of 30 days beginning with Sunday would be:
questions.solution:
A 30-day month starting with Sunday contains 5 Sundays and 25 other days.
$$\text{Total attendance} = 5 \times 410 + 25 \times 230 = 2050 + 5750 = 7800$$
$$\text{Average attendance} = \frac{7800}{30} = 260$$

If the average score of students in section A is 20% more than that of students in section B, then what is the average score of students in section A (correct to one decimal place)?

$$50(6x) + 62(5x) = (50 + 62) \times 75 = 112 \times 75 = 8400$$
$$300x + 310x = 8400 \implies 610x = 8400 \implies x = \frac{840}{61}$$
$$\text{Average score of A} = 6x = 6 \times \frac{840}{61} = \frac{5040}{61} \approx 82.6$$

questions.questionText: According to Raghav, his weight is more than 64 kg but less than 74 kg. His sister does not agree with Raghav and she thinks that his weight is more than 60 kg but less than 69 kg. His mother's view is that his weight cannot be more than 68 kg. His father's view is that his weight cannot be more than 67 kg. If all are them are correct in their estimation, then what is the average of different probable weights of Raghav measured (in kg)?
questions.solution:
Raghav: $> 64$ and $< 74$.
Sister: $> 60$ and $< 69$.
Mother: $\le 68$.
Father: $\le 67$.
Common range: $64 < \text{weight} \le 67$. Probable integer weights $= 65, 66, 67$.
$$\text{Average} = \frac{65 + 66 + 67}{3} = 66\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: There are 3 groups of persons - male, female and children. There are 20 males and the number of females and children taken together is 4 more than that of the males. The average weight of males is 54 kg, that of females is 49 kg and that of children is 30 kg. If the average weight of the whole group is 48.25 kg, then what is the difference between the number of females and the number of children?
questions.solution:
$M = 20$, $F + C = 20 + 4 = 24$. Total $= 44$ persons.
$$\text{Total weight} = 44 \times 48.25 = 2123\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Weight of males} = 20 \times 54 = 1080\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Weight of (F + C)} = 2123 - 1080 = 1043\text{ kg}$$
$$49F + 30C = 1043 \quad \text{and} \quad F + C = 24$$
$$49F + 30(24 - F) = 1043 \implies 19F + 720 = 1043 \implies 19F = 323 \implies F = 17$$
$$C = 24 - 17 = 7$$
$$\text{Difference } |F - C| = 17 - 7 = 10$$

questions.questionText: In an examination, the average score of a student was 67.6. If he would have got 27 more marks in Mathematics, 10 more marks in Computer Science, 18 more marks in History and retained the same marks in other subjects, then his average score would have been 72.6. How many papers were there in the examination?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total extra marks} = 27 + 10 + 18 = 55$$
$$\text{Increase in average} = 72.6 - 67.6 = 5$$
$$\text{Number of papers} = \frac{55}{5} = 11$$

questions.questionText: When 2 is subtracted from each of the given n number, then the sum of the numbers so obtained is 102. When 5 is subtracted from each of them, then the sum of the numbers so obtained is 12. What is the average of the given n numbers?

The numbers 2, 3, 4 and 5 occurs (k + 5k), (5k - 7), (2k - 3) and (k + 2) times, respectively. The average of the numbers is 2.85. Later on, the number 2 was replaced by 6 in all the places. What is the average of the new numbers?
questions.solution:
Frequencies: for $2$ is $6k$, for $3$ is $5k-7$, for $4$ is $2k-3$, for $5$ is $k+2$.
Sum of frequencies $N = 14k - 8$.
Total sum $= 2(6k) + 3(5k-7) + 4(2k-3) + 5(k+2) = 12k + 15k - 21 + 8k - 12 + 5k + 10 = 40k - 23$.
$$\frac{40k - 23}{14k - 8} = 2.85 \implies 40k - 23 = 39.9k - 22.8 \implies 0.1k = 0.2 \implies k = 2$$
For $k = 2$, frequency of $2$ is $6(2) = 12$. Total count $N = 14(2) - 8 = 20$.
Replacing $2$ with $6$ adds $4$ to each of the $12$ instances, adding $12 \times 4 = 48$.
$$\text{Increase in average} = \frac{48}{20} = 2.4$$
$$\text{New average} = 2.85 + 2.4 = 5.25$$

questions.questionText: The average of x occurring 5 times and y occurring 7 times is 37. Also the average of x occurring 7 times and y occurring 5 times is 35. The value of x/6 is:
questions.solution:
$$5x + 7y = 12 \times 37 = 444$$
$$7x + 5y = 12 \times 35 = 420$$
Adding equations: $12x + 12y = 864 \implies x + y = 72$.
Subtracting equations: $2x - 2y = -24 \implies x - y = -12$.
$$2x = 60 \implies x = 30$$
$$\frac{x}{6} = \frac{30}{6} = 5$$

questions.questionText: In an examination, average marks of a student per paper were 71. If he would have obtained 35 more marks in sciences; 11 more marks in history and 4 more marks in computer science, his average marks per paper would have been 76. How many papers were there in the examination?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total extra marks} = 35 + 11 + 4 = 50$$
$$\text{Increase in average} = 76 - 71 = 5$$
$$\text{Number of papers} = \frac{50}{5} = 10$$

questions.questionText: The average weight of 30 persons of group A is 3 kg more than the average weight of 25 persons of group B. The average weight of 25 persons of group B is 2.5 kg more than the average weight of 20 persons of group C. If the total weight of 30 persons of group A is 1725 kg, then what will be the average weight of the persons of group A and group C taken together (in kg)?
questions.solution:
$$\text{Average of A} = \frac{1725}{30} = 57.5\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Average of B} = 57.5 - 3 = 54.5\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Average of C} = 54.5 - 2.5 = 52\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Total weight of C (20 persons)} = 20 \times 52 = 1040\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Total weight (A + C)} = 1725 + 1040 = 2765\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Combined average (50 persons)} = \frac{2765}{50} = 55.3\text{ kg}$$

Stock C represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock D represents the remaining 30% of the portfolio and has a negative-return of 5%. What is the average return of the portfolio?

Stock C represents the remaining 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. What is the average return percentage of the portfolio?
The average of 25 integers is zero. What is the maximum possible number of positive integers?
questions.solution:
Sum of 25 integers $= 25 \times 0 = 0$.
If 24 integers are positive, their sum can be cancelled by a single negative integer whose magnitude equals the sum of the 24 positive integers.
$$\text{Maximum possible positive integers} = 24$$

questions.questionText: The average of 27 numbers is zero. Out of them, how many may be greater than zero, at the most?
questions.solution:
Sum of 27 numbers $= 0$. At most, 26 numbers can be positive, balanced by 1 negative number.
$$\text{Maximum numbers greater than zero} = 26$$

questions.questionText: In a team of seven members, the average age of six of the members is 42 years while the age of the seventh member of the team is 36 years more than the average age of all the seven members taken together. Find the age (in years) of the seventh member of the team.
questions.solution:
Let overall average $= A$. Seventh member $= A + 36$.
$$6 \times 42 + (A + 36) = 7A \implies 252 + 36 = 6A \implies 6A = 288 \implies A = 48$$
$$\text{Age of 7th member} = 48 + 36 = 84\text{ years}$$

questions.questionText: The average weight of Rohan and his three friends is 62 kg. If Rohan's weight is 8 kg more than the average weight of his three friends, what is Rohan's weight (in kg)?
questions.solution:
Total weight of 4 persons $= 4 \times 62 = 248\text{ kg}$.
Let average weight of 3 friends $= F$. Rohan $= F + 8$.
$$3F + (F + 8) = 248 \implies 4F = 240 \implies F = 60$$
$$\text{Rohan's weight} = 60 + 8 = 68\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: The average weight of the first thirteen persons among fourteen persons is 78 kg. The weight of the 14th person is 39 kg more than the average weight of all the fourteen persons. Find the weight of the 14th person.
questions.solution:
Let overall average $= A$. 14th person $= A + 39$.
$$13 \times 78 + (A + 39) = 14A \implies 1014 + 39 = 13A \implies 13A = 1053 \implies A = 81\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Weight of 14th person} = 81 + 39 = 120\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: 20 Students of a college went to a hotel. 19 of them spent ₹ 175 each on their meal and the 20th student spent ₹ 19 more than the average of all the 20. Find the total money spent by them.
questions.solution:
Let average spent by 20 students $= A$. 20th student spent $A + 19$.
$$19 \times 175 + (A + 19) = 20A \implies 3325 + 19 = 19A \implies 19A = 3344 \implies A = 176$$
$$\text{Total money spent} = 20 \times 176 = ₹3520$$

questions.questionText: Eleven friends spent ₹ 18 each on a tour and the twelfth friend spent ₹11 less than the average expenditure of all twelve of them. What is the total money spent by twelve friends?
questions.solution:
Let overall average $= A$. 12th friend spent $A - 11$.
$$11 \times 18 + (A - 11) = 12A \implies 198 - 11 = 11A \implies 11A = 187 \implies A = 17$$
$$\text{Total money spent} = 12 \times 17 = ₹204$$

questions.questionText: The average weight of P and his three friends is 55 kg. If P is 4 kg more than the average weight of his three friends, what is P's weight (in kg)?
questions.solution:
Total weight of 4 $= 4 \times 55 = 220\text{ kg}$.
Let average weight of 3 friends $= F$. $P = F + 4$.
$$3F + (F + 4) = 220 \implies 4F = 216 \implies F = 54$$
$$P = 54 + 4 = 58\text{ kg}$$

questions.questionText: There are 90 students in a hostel. Due to new admissions, 30 new students join the mess and the daily expenses of the mess increases by ₹ 560, while the average expenditure per head diminishes by ₹ 10. What was the original daily expenditure (in ₹) of the mess?
questions.solution:
Let original average expenditure per head $= x$.
Original daily expenditure $= 90x$.
$$120(x - 10) = 90x + 560 \implies 120x - 1200 = 90x + 560 \implies 30x = 1760$$
$$\text{Original expenditure} = 90x = 3 \times (30x) = 3 \times 1760 = ₹5,280$$

questions.questionText: The average monthly income of A and B is ₹5,050, the average monthly income of B and C is ₹6,250, and the average monthly income of A and C is ₹5,200. What is the sum of the monthly incomes (in ₹) of A, B and C?

There are 75 students in the hostel. Due to new admissions, 15 new students join the mess, and the daily expenses of the mess increased by ₹ 240, while the average expenditure per head diminished by 5. What was the original expenditure (in ₹) of the mess?
questions.solution:
Let original average per head $= x$.
Original daily expenditure $= 75x$.
$$90(x - 5) = 75x + 240 \implies 90x - 450 = 75x + 240 \implies 15x = 690 \implies x = 46$$
$$\text{Original expenditure} = 75 \times 46 = ₹3,450$$

questions.questionText: 8 kg of maize costing Rs.51 per kg, is mixed with 9 kg of maize costing Rs.68 per kg. The average per kg price of mixed maize is:
questions.solution:
$$\text{Total cost} = 8 \times 51 + 9 \times 68 = 408 + 612 = \text{Rs. } 1020$$
$$\text{Total quantity} = 8 + 9 = 17\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Average price per kg} = \frac{1020}{17} = \text{Rs. } 60$$
